2: // A dependency-free stand-in for eslint and prettier, so the Chapter 6 hooks

6: import { join } from 'node:path';
7: 
8: const fix = process.argv.includes('--fix');
9: const targets = process.argv.slice(2).filter((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
10: 
11: function walk(dir) {
12:   return readdirSync(dir).flatMap((e) => {
13:     const p = join(dir, e);
14:     if (statSync(p).isDirectory()) return walk(p);
15:     return p.endsWith('.js') ? [p] : [];
16:   });
17: }
18: 
19: const files = targets.length ? targets : [...walk('src'), ...walk('tests')];
20: let problems = 0;

25:   if (!after.endsWith('\n')) after += '\n';
26:   after = after.replace(/\n{3,}$/, '\n');
27:   if (after !== before) {
28:     if (fix) writeFileSync(f, after);

31: }

33: if (problems && !fix) {

35:   process.exit(1);

part.text: - **Low — Invalid user IDs are silently accepted** (`src/api/routes.js:9–10`). Both handlers pass `Number(req.params.id)` directly to their services without validation. An ID such as `"abc"` becomes `NaN`, so the callback reports success with `null` or `[]`, rather than an invalid-input error. Validate the converted ID before calling the service and report validation failures through `cb(err)`. Existing service tests and the route smoke check cover no malformed-ID cases.
